toc.label: Structural Intervention Distance (SID)
toc.definition: A new graph-based (pre-)metric that compares two DAGs based on whether they imply the same interventional distributions, rather than on edge overlap.
sub_questions: How does SID differ conceptually from edge-counting metrics like SHD?
What graphical criterion characterizes when SID assigns a pair of nodes a mismatch?
In what sense is SID a pre-metric rather than a true metric?
How does SID extend to CPDAGs and other graph types?

toc.label: Comparing Estimated and True Causal Graphs
toc.definition: Given a true causal DAG and an estimate, we want to measure the closeness of the causal statements they imply.
sub_questions: Why is edge-based comparison insufficient for assessing causal accuracy?
What downstream causal statements should a good distance measure preserve?

toc.label: Structural Hamming Distance (SHD)
toc.definition: A distance between two PDAGs that counts how many edges must be added, removed, or reoriented to transform one into the other.
sub_questions: What edge-level operations does SHD count?
Why can two SHD-close DAGs disagree strongly on implied causal effects?

toc.label: Intervention Distributions
toc.definition: A distribution is Markov with respect to a DAG iff it factorizes according to the graph, which in turn determines its interventional distributions.
sub_questions: What is the relationship between Markov factorization and interventional distributions?
How are interventional distributions computed from a DAG via the truncated factorization?

toc.label: Motivation and Definition of SID
toc.definition: SID is defined by checking, for each ordered pair of nodes, whether the true and estimated DAG imply the same interventional distribution of one node under intervention on the other.
sub_questions: Why is SID defined pairwise over ordered node pairs?
What counts as a 'correct' intervention-effect prediction under this definition?

toc.label: Equivalent Graphical Formulation
toc.definition: A graphical criterion equivalent to the interventional definition of SID that avoids explicitly evaluating intervention distributions.
sub_questions: What graphical condition on parent sets and paths replaces direct computation of intervention distributions?
Why does this reformulation make SID tractable to compute?

toc.label: Metric Properties of SID
toc.definition: Investigation of metric-like properties of SID, including bounds expressed in terms of the number of nodes in the graph.
sub_questions: Does SID satisfy metric axioms such as symmetry and the triangle inequality?
What are the known upper and lower bounds on SID relative to the number of nodes?
How does SID relate to SHD under specific graph conditions?

toc.label: SID between a DAG and a CPDAG
toc.definition: An extension of SID for comparing a true DAG to an estimated CPDAG, since some causal inference methods only output CPDAGs.
sub_questions: How is SID aggregated across all DAGs represented by a CPDAG?
What causal inference methods produce CPDAG estimates that motivate this extension?

toc.label: SID between a CPDAG and a DAG or CPDAG
toc.definition: An extension for settings where the true graph itself is only identifiable up to a CPDAG, e.g. linear Gaussian SEMs with equal error variances.
sub_questions: Why can the true DAG be unidentifiable even when the causal structure is known?
How does SID adapt when both the true and estimated graphs are CPDAGs?

toc.label: Penalizing Additional Edges
toc.definition: A modification of SID that penalizes estimated DAGs with strictly more edges than the true DAG, which otherwise can receive an SID of zero.
sub_questions: Why can an overly dense estimated DAG achieve a perfect SID score?
What penalty term is added to discourage superfluous edges?

toc.label: Symmetrization of SID
toc.definition: A symmetric version of SID for comparing two DAGs where neither can be seen as ground truth for the other.
sub_questions: How is a symmetric distance constructed from the inherently asymmetric SID?
In what comparison scenarios is symmetrization needed?

toc.label: Alternative Adjustment Sets
toc.definition: Discussion of adjustment sets other than the parent set, which is used in this work because it is easy to compute and depends only on local neighbourhood.
sub_questions: What tradeoffs exist between parent-set adjustment and other valid adjustment sets?
Why does parent-set adjustment depend only on local neighbourhood information?

toc.label: Hidden Variables (Future Work)
toc.definition: Future work on the case where some variables are unobserved, so not all intervention distributions are identifiable from the true DAG.
sub_questions: How should SID be redefined when latent confounders make some interventions unidentifiable?
What graphical model should replace the DAG in this setting?

toc.label: Multiple Interventions (Future Work)
toc.definition: Future work extending SID beyond single-node interventions to compare predictions under simultaneous interventions on multiple variables.
sub_questions: How does comparing multi-node intervention distributions change the graphical criterion?
Does the computational tractability of SID survive this generalization?

toc.label: SID versus SHD Simulation
toc.definition: A simulation study sampling pairs of random DAGs and computing both SID and SHD between them to compare their behavior.
sub_questions: How do SID and SHD diverge across different random graph models?
What does the empirical relationship reveal about the informativeness of each metric?

toc.label: Comparing Causal Inference Methods
toc.definition: Simulations comparing causal inference methods by evaluating their output graphs against sparse random ground-truth DAGs using SID.
sub_questions: Do method rankings differ when evaluated by SID versus SHD?
Which methods perform well under intervention-based evaluation but poorly under edge-based evaluation?

toc.label: Scalability of the SID
toc.definition: An empirical report of processor time needed to compute SID between two random graphs as the number of nodes grows.
sub_questions: How does SID computation time scale with the number of nodes?
Is the empirical runtime consistent with the algorithm's theoretical complexity?

toc.label: Implementation of SID
toc.definition: A sketch of the implementation of the Structural Intervention Distance, with full algorithmic details presented separately.
sub_questions: What are the main computational steps in implementing SID?
How are the graphical criteria from the equivalent formulation translated into code?

toc.label: DAG Terminology
toc.definition: A summary of well-known graph-theoretic facts and terminology about directed acyclic graphs used throughout the paper.
sub_questions: What DAG concepts (parents, ancestors, d-separation) are prerequisites for defining SID?
How do these definitions extend to PDAGs and CPDAGs?

toc.label: Proof: Equivalence of Definitions
toc.definition: Proof establishing the equivalence between the interventional definition of SID and its graphical formulation.
sub_questions: What is the key lemma linking intervention distributions to the graphical criterion?
Where does the proof rely on the Markov property versus faithfulness?

toc.label: Proof: SID for Superset Estimates
toc.definition: Proof that when the estimated DAG's edges and parent structure meet certain superset conditions, the SID is zero.
sub_questions: Under what edge-superset conditions does the proof guarantee SID equals zero?
How does this proof connect to the additional-edges penalty discussion?

toc.label: Proof: SID and SHD Relationship
toc.definition: Proof of the relationship between SHD and SID, including that a zero SHD implies identical parent sets for every node.
sub_questions: What does zero SHD imply about parent sets, and how does that bound SID?
Are there cases where small SHD does not imply small SID?

toc.label: Causal Effects in Linear Gaussian SEMs
toc.definition: Derivation of the covariance matrix and causal effects for a linear Gaussian structural equation model with known parameters.
sub_questions: How is the covariance matrix of a linear Gaussian SEM computed from its structural coefficients?
How are these closed-form effects used in simulations to compute SID?

toc.label: SID Algorithms
toc.definition: Pseudo code of two algorithms for computing the SID given two adjacency matrices.
sub_questions: What are the inputs and outputs of the two presented algorithms?
What is the computational complexity of each algorithm step?
